criteria: Disclosure policy, payment terms, severity rubric and legal opinion summary published and intake live, rubric accepted by the technical reviewer
At least 5 outside research teams submitting findings, confirmed by those teams to the technical reviewer
milestones.name: Broker open

criteria: At least 25 distinct medium-or-higher findings from at least 5 outside research teams fixed by at least 10 outside teams, each fix a patched commit or upgraded contract checked by the technical reviewer
At least 10 of the fixing teams hold over $10M onchain (value query linked), checked by the technical reviewer
At least 10 of the findings are high or critical, checked by the technical reviewer
milestones.name: First fixes

criteria: At least 100 distinct medium-or-higher findings fixed in total, each a patched commit or upgraded contract, at least 25 high or critical and at least 25 in code with no live bounty program, from at least 10 outside research teams, 2 of them from this list: OpenZeppelin, Trail of Bits, ChainSecurity, Spearbit, Consensys Diligence, Sigma Prime, Certora, Cyfrin, Zellic, Ackee Blockchain, Runtime Verification, Nethermind Security, checked by the technical reviewer
The fixes span at least 30 outside teams each holding over $10M onchain, at least 10 of them over $50M (value query linked), checked by the technical reviewer
Median time from intake to the affected team acknowledging under 7 days, on the broker's public metrics page, checked by the technical reviewer

At least $250,000 paid to outside researchers for findings brokered under this initiative, by at least 10 outside teams or bounty programs, and at least $30,000 of broker revenue from outside parties, grants excluded, shown by payment records to the technical reviewer
milestones.name: At scale

criteria: At least $500,000 paid to outside researchers in total for findings brokered under this initiative, by at least 10 outside teams or bounty programs, at least $100,000 of it for code with no live bounty program, each paid after the payer had the full finding, shown by payment records to the technical reviewer

At least $70,000 of broker revenue in total from outside teams, researchers or bounty programs, grants excluded, checked by the technical reviewer, plus a plan to run 12 months past the grant without grants
milestones.name: Paying for itself

sections.existing:
- [Zero Day Initiative](https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/about/): Web2's trusted broker since 2005. It pays researchers, then gives the vendor the details and a 120-day deadline ([policy](https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/advisories/disclosure_policy/)).
- [SEAL 911](https://securityalliance.org/seal-911): a free emergency hotline that has coordinated over 200 war rooms for active or imminent incidents. The broker handles findings not under active exploit.
sections.hard_req:
1. **Disclosure never depends on payment.** The affected team receives the full finding at first contact, with no condition, before any payment request.
2. **Terms first.** Payment terms, the same for every team, are published before any team is contacted. A law firm's opinion on the model goes to the technical reviewer, with its summary published, before the first payment request.
3. A finding goes only to the teams that must fix it, never sold or licensed to anyone else.
4. Nothing about an unfixed finding is published, including which team is slow to respond.
5. Every finding is validated with a working proof of concept before any team is contacted.
6. Researchers may stay unnamed in public.
7. **Outside means unaffiliated:** no shared owner, staff or funding with the selected team. A payment or fix counts only when payer and researcher are also unaffiliated with each other, and each finding is a separate root cause.
8. Ethereum and L2 code only.
9. **A business that pays for itself.** The broker is a for-profit company that charges for its service, with a business model in the bid that covers its costs after the grant.
sections.in_scope:
The goal: validated findings get fixed, including in unmaintained code, and researchers get paid, bounty or no bounty. Bidders have complete freedom in how they get there, including their own milestones, within the hard requirements below. This RFP is a starting point and will change; the final milestones are agreed with the selected team.

One possible approach, the one the milestones below follow:

- Build relationships with real bug hunters, validate their exploits, and take each finding to the owner with the full details and an offer to help fix it.
- Charge for it: fees from teams, a cut of researcher payments, commissions on bounty submissions it files and defends, or another model.
- Keep a working line to SEAL's war rooms for findings that turn into live attacks.
- Use the security contacts published under the companion security-contact RFP without depending on them.
sections.out_scope:
- Bug hunting itself.
- Whitehat rescues of funds at risk ([separate RFP](https://initiatives.thedao.fund/initiative/an-open-bug-bounty-program-for-all-of-ethereum-white-hat-res) on this board).
- Bugs in shared code where several teams must fix together (the companion coordinated-patching RFP).
sections.who:
An independent for-profit company: an audit firm with an AI bug-hunting pipeline, a bounty platform, or a new firm. The best pitch answers one question: why will researchers and teams both trust you? A clear connection to SEAL, whose war rooms bring together major security crews, is a strong plus. Nobody is pre-selected.

Drafted by TheDAO Security Fund from a conversation with EthSec (ethsecurity.org) and Consensys. Consensys Diligence may bid. A fix counts toward the milestones of only one initiative on this board. EthSec, TheDAO Security Fund and Giveth will not bid.
sections.why:
Every valid finding left unfixed waits for the next attacker to find it. Users are safer when someone both sides trust owns the job of getting it fixed.

- Bounties work where programs exist: [Immunefi](https://immunefi.com/) has paid researchers over $140M. Code with no bounty, no maintainer or a program that never answers has no such path.
- Without a broker we expect researchers to drop findings rather than chase unbountied teams, since a lone researcher asking for payment risks looking like an extortionist.

initiative.summary: In the age of AI, team inboxes fill with junk bug reports, so whether a real bug gets fixed comes down to who sends it and whether the team trusts them. This RFP seeds a for-profit broker that builds relationships with real bug hunters and validates their exploits. It takes serious findings to teams across Ethereum that trust it, sees them fixed and the researcher paid, and lives on its fees.
initiative.title: RFP: A Bug Broker That Gets Ethereum Bugs Fixed and Researchers Paid, Bounty or No Bounty
